key_insight: EHR-RobustGym shows that clinical AI agents can produce plausible but unsupported answers when EHR data are noisy, and it benchmarks tools to improve evidence-grounded reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This matters for hospitals because robust clinical agents need to handle missing, noisy, or conflicting record evidence without overconfidently answering queries.
method: Built a scalable interactive benchmark on MIMIC-IV EHR data.
Created 5,486 Clean-Noise pairs across six clinical intents and multiple noise types.
Enabled SQL/Python execution and outcome verification for evaluation and training.
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans 365K patients and over 500M records, and evaluated models saw average task success drop from 62.2% on clean questions to 37.9% on noisy questions.
watch_item: Results come from benchmarked EHR tasks, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation against local data quality, workflows, and safety requirements.
paper_title: EHR-RobustGym: Benchmarking and Training Agents for Robust Clinical Reasoning
